description:
Design a 4-bit DRAM cell with read and write operations. The cell should be able to store a 4-bit value and allow reading the stored value. The DRAM cell will have the following inputs:
- `clk`: Clock input
- `we`: Write enable (1 for write, 0 for read)
- `data_in`: 4-bit input data to be written to the cell
- `data_out`: 4-bit output data read from the cell

When `we` is high, the `data_in` should be stored in the cell on the rising edge of `clk`. When `we` is low, the `data_out` should reflect the stored value.
code:
module DRAM_Cell (
    input wire clk,
    input wire we,
    input wire [3:0] data_in,
    output reg [3:0] data_out
);
    reg [3:0] memory;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (we) begin
            memory <= data_in; // Write operation
        end
    end

    always @(negedge clk) begin
        if (!we) begin
            data_out <= memory; // Read operation
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Watchdog Timer that resets a system if it does not receive a reset signal within a specified timeout period. The timer should have an input clock signal, a reset signal that is activated when the system is functioning correctly, and an output signal that asserts when the timer reaches its timeout. Specify a timeout period of 10 clock cycles. The timer should also have a way to be stopped and restarted.
code:
module watchdog_timer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire start,
    output reg timeout
);
    reg [3:0] counter; // 4-bit counter for 10 cycles

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            counter <= 4'b0000;
            timeout <= 1'b0;
        end else if (start) begin
            if (counter < 4'd9) begin
                counter <= counter + 1'b1;
                timeout <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                timeout <= 1'b1; // Timeout reached
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 2-to-1 multiplexer using Verilog. The multiplexer should have two data inputs (A and B), one select input (S), and one output (Y). The output Y should reflect A when S is 0, and B when S is 1.

Design a Verilog module for a simple gradient descent optimizer that adjusts a variable `x` based on a given gradient `grad`. The optimizer should operate on a clock signal and update the value of `x` on every positive edge of the clock. The learning rate should be a constant value defined in the module. The initial value of `x` should be set to zero. The module should output the updated value of `x` after each clock cycle.
code:
module gradient_descent_optimizer(
    input wire clk,
    input wire [15:0] grad,
    output reg [15:0] x
);
    parameter LEARNING_RATE = 16'h0001; // Set learning rate

    initial begin
        x = 16'h0000; // Initial value of x
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        x <= x - (grad * LEARNING_RATE); // Update x using gradient
    end
endmodule

description:
Design an 8-bit DRAM cell that has the following functionality:
- The cell can be written to when the write enable signal (`we`) is high, and the input data is provided on the `data_in` bus.
- The cell can be read when the `we` signal is low, and the output data should be available on the `data_out` bus.

    output reg [7:0] data_out
);

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            memory <= 8'b0; // Reset the memory
        end else if (we) begin
            memory <= data_in; // Write data to memory
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (!we) begin
            data_out <= memory; // Read data from memory
        end

Design a combinational logic circuit that implements the Black-Scholes option pricing formula. The circuit should take the following inputs:
- `S`: Current stock price (fixed-point representation, 16 bits)
- `K`: Strike price (fixed-point representation, 16 bits)
- `T`: Time to expiration (in years, fixed-point representation, 8 bits)
- `r`: Risk-free interest rate (fixed-point representation, 8 bits)
- `sigma`: Volatility of the stock (fixed-point representation, 8 bits)

The output should be the calculated option price (fixed-point representation, 32 bits) using the Black-Scholes model for a European call option.

The formula for the Black-Scholes model is:
C = S * N(d1) - K * e^(-rT) * N(d2)

Where:
- d1 = (ln(S/K) + (r + (sigma^2)/2) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T))
- d2 = d1 - sigma * sqrt(T)
- N(x) is the cumulative distribution function of the standard normal distribution.

Make necessary assumptions for fixed-point arithmetic.

Design a JK latch using Verilog. The JK latch has two inputs J and K, a clock input CLK, and two outputs Q and Qn. The latch should toggle its output based on the values of J and K at the rising edge of CLK.
code:
module JK_latch (
    input J,
    input K,
    input CLK,
    output reg Q,
    output Qn
);
    assign Qn = ~Q;

    always @(posedge CLK) begin
        if (J && ~K) begin
            Q <= 1; // Set
        end else if (~J && K) begin
            Q <= 0; // Reset
        end else if (J && K) begin
            Q <= ~Q; // Toggle
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a digital phase shifter that takes a 3-bit input representing a phase value and a control signal. Design a 16-bit serializer that takes a 16-bit parallel input and serializes it to a 1-bit output. The module should have a clock and reset input. On each clock tick, it should output the next bit of the input. After all 16 bits have been output, it should reset and start over.

    input wire reset,
    input wire [15:0] parallel_in,
    output reg serial_out
);

            serial_out <= 0;
        end else begin

                count <= count + 1;
            end else begin
                count <= 0; // Reset count after 16 bits
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a Verilog module that performs LU decomposition on a 2x2 matrix. The input will be a 2x2 matrix represented as four 8-bit unsigned integers, and the output will be two 2x2 matrices L and U, also represented as four 8-bit unsigned integers each. The L matrix will be a lower triangular matrix, and the U matrix will be an upper triangular matrix.
code:
module LU_Decomposition (
    input [7:0] a11, a12,
    input [7:0] a21, a22,
    output [7:0] l11, l12,
    output [7:0] l21, l22,
    output [7:0] u11, u12,
    output [7:0] u21, u22
);
    assign l11 = 8'd1; // L11 = 1
    assign l12 = 8'd0; // L12 = 0
    assign l21 = a21;  // L21 = A21
    assign l22 = (a22 - (l21 * u12)) / l11; // L22 = A22 - L21 * U12 / L11

    assign u11 = a11; // U11 = A11
    assign u12 = a12; // U12 = A12
    assign u21 = 8'd0; // U21 = 0
    assign u22 = a22 - (l21 * u12); // U22 = A22 - L21 * U12

endmodule

);

description:

3. An enable input that allows the flip-flop to store the input value (D) when high and hold the previous value when low.

code:

    input wire reset,
    input wire enable,
    input wire D,
    output reg Q
);

    if (reset) begin
        Q <= 0; // Asynchronous reset

endmodule

description: A Watchdog timer is a hardware timer that is used to detect and recover from computer malfunctions. Your task is to design a Watchdog timer that resets itself if it receives a "kick" (a signal to reset the timer) within a specified timeout period. If the timer reaches the timeout limit without being kicked, it will generate a reset signal. The timer should have a clock input, a kick input, and an output for the reset signal. The timer can be configured with a parameter that sets the timeout period.
code:
module watchdog_timer #(parameter TIMEOUT = 4) (  
    input wire clk,  
    input wire kick,  
    output reg reset  
);  
    reg [3:0] count; // 4-bit counter to count clock cycles  

    always @(posedge clk) begin  
        if (kick) begin  
            count <= 0; // Reset count on kick  
            reset <= 0; // No reset when kicked  
        end else begin  
            if (count < TIMEOUT) begin  
                count <= count + 1; // Increment count  
                reset <= 0; // No reset yet  
            end else begin  
                reset <= 1; // Generate reset signal after timeout  
            end  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

description: Design a 16-bit ADC controller that takes a 16-bit digital input value and converts it to an 8-bit digital output value by dividing the input by 256. description: Design a simple interrupt controller that has a register to hold the interrupt status. The controller should have a clock input and a reset input. On reset, the interrupt status should be cleared. On the rising edge of the clock, if an interrupt request signal is high, the corresponding bit in the interrupt status register should be set. The controller should have an output that indicates if there are any pending interrupts.
code:
module interrupt_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [3:0] int_req,
    output reg [3:0] int_status,
    output reg int_pending
);

always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
    if (rst) begin
        int_status <= 4'b0000;
        int_pending <= 1'b0;
    end else begin
        int_status <= int_status | int_req;
        int_pending <= |int_status; // Check if any interrupt is set
    end
end

endmodule

description: Design a SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface) master controller that can transmit and receive data from a slave device.     input wire cpha,             // Clock phase

    output reg mosi,             // Master Out Slave In

    output reg cs_n,             // Chip select (active low)
    output reg busy,             // Indicates the controller is busy
    output reg [7:0] rx_data     // Data received from slave
);

    reg [2:0] state;            // State machine
    reg [2:0] bit_count;        // Bit counter for transmission
    reg [7:0] shift_reg;        // Shift register for transmission/receiving

    localparam IDLE = 3'b000, 
               START = 3'b001, 
               TRANSFER = 3'b010, 
               STOP = 3'b011;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            busy <= 0;
            cs_n <= 1; // CS is high (inactive)
            sclk <= 0;
            bit_count <= 0;
            rx_data <= 0;
            mosi <= 0;
            miso <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        cs_n <= 0; // Activate chip select
                        shift_reg <= tx_data; // Load data to send
                        bit_count <= 0; // Reset bit counter
                        state <= START;
                        busy <= 1;
                    end
                end
                
                START: begin
                    if (cpha == 0) sclk <= 1; // Set clock high
                    state <= TRANSFER; // Move to transfer state
                end

                TRANSFER: begin
                    if (bit_count < 8) begin
                        sclk <= ~sclk; // Toggle clock
                        if (sclk) begin // On rising edge
                            mosi <= shift_reg[7]; // Send MSB
                            miso <= 0; // Assuming slave drives miso
                            shift_reg <= {shift_reg[6:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left
                            bit_count <= bit_count + 1; // Increment bit count
                        end else begin // On falling edge
                            rx_data <= {rx_data[6:0], miso}; // Receive data
                        end
                    end else begin
                        state <= STOP; // Move to stop state after 8 bits
                    end
                end
                
                STOP: begin
                    cs_n <= 1; // Deactivate chip select
                    busy <= 0;
                    state <= IDLE; // Go back to idle
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

);

        IDLE: begin
            tx <= 1; // idle high
            if (start) begin
                state <= START_BIT;
                bit_index <= 0; // reset bit index
            end

        START_BIT: begin
            tx <= 0; // start bit
            state <= DATA_BITS;
        end
        DATA_BITS: begin

            if (bit_index == 7) begin
                state <= STOP_BIT;
            end else begin

    input wire rst,
    input wire req_ch1,
    input wire req_ch2,
    output reg done_ch1,
    output reg done_ch2
);
    reg [1:0] state; // 00: idle, 01: transferring ch1, 10: transferring ch2

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= 2'b00;
            done_ch1 <= 0;
            done_ch2 <= 0;
        end else begin

                    done_ch2 <= 0;
                    if (req_ch1) begin

                    state <= 2'b00; // return to idle

);

            QN <= 1;

module kalman_filter (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [15:0] measurement,
    input [15:0] process_noise,
    input [15:0] measurement_noise,
    output reg [15:0] estimate
);

reg [15:0] x_prev; // previous state estimate
reg [15:0] p_prev; // previous estimation error covariance
reg [15:0] k;      // Kalman gain
reg [15:0] p;      // estimation error covariance

always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        estimate <= 16'b0;
        x_prev <= 16'b0;
        p_prev <= 16'b1; // initial covariance
    end else begin
        // Prediction step
        x_prev <= estimate; // Use the current estimate as the previous state
        p_prev <= p_prev + process_noise; // Update covariance

        // Update step
        k <= p_prev / (p_prev + measurement_noise); // Calculate Kalman gain
        estimate <= x_prev + k * (measurement - x_prev); // Update estimate
        p <= (16'b1 - k) * p_prev; // Update error covariance
    end
end

endmodule

    input rst,
    input bit_in,
    output reg detected
);

        if (rst) begin
            state <= S0;
            detected <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                S0: begin
                    if (bit_in) state <= S1; // 1 detected
                    else state <= S0;       // 0 detected
                    detected <= 0;

                    if (bit_in) state <= S2; // 1 detected

                    detected <= 0;

                        detected <= 0;
                    end else begin

            endcase
